content:
maria: Quick UX question — on the compact "form row" we added in the Routes dashboard: should we surface inline errors or keep a single summary at the top? Screenshot: https://img.example/route-form-compact.png alex: my vote is inline for required/missing field errors (so people can fix in context). summary for validation that affects multiple fields. jess: agree with alex. Inline = faster fix. But we should avoid visual noise when several fields are invalid. Maybe inline + a condensed summary pill that appears when >2 errors. dinesh: accessibility: if we keep inline, make sure each inline error has aria-describedby pointing to the error text and the container uses role="alert" for assistive tech. For summary, include a skip link: "Jump to first error". sam: +1 on condensed summary pill. Also, for required markers — are we settled on asterisk + "(required)" in the form legend? a11y folks prefer explicit text. :thinking_face: maria: want minimal visual weight. Proposal: use an asterisk visually, but include hidden text for screen readers: required. That keeps density low but stays explicit. Thoughts? jess: prefer the hidden text approach. Also recommend `aria-required="true"` on the input element itself. aria-bot: Accessibility checklist reminder: - Provide aria-required on required controls - Link inline errors via aria-describedby - Ensure error summary is keyboard focusable and announces number of errors when focused - Color alone must not indicate error (add icon or bold label) alex: switching topic: destructive action on that screen — the table has a delete icon that currently triggers a simple confirm modal. Product asked for a stronger guard for shared routes. Options: 1) typed confirmation (type resource name), 2) checkbox + secondary confirmation button, 3) delay + undo toast. dinesh: typed confirmation is strongest from a safety POV but reduces speed. For shared routes I’d prefer typed confirm. For single-user quick deletes we can use a checkbox. sam: copy suggestion for the modal: "Permanently delete route \"/customer-signup\". This action cannot be undone. To confirm, type the route path below." Primary button label: "Delete route permanently" (red) jess: can we avoid that long primary? maybe just "Delete permanently" and show path above so copy stays scannable. maria: UX tradeoff: typed confirmations block muscle-memory mistakes at cost of friction. Proposal: typed confirm for routes that are shared or have >1 active service attached. For everything else, checkbox + red button + undo toast. alex: sounds reasonable. Implementation note: modal body should include small footprint help text: "This will remove this route from all services using it." And surface dependent services count. dinesh: dev note: when using typed-confirm, validate client-side and server-side. Don’t rely on UI only. Also add `aria-live="polite"` region for validation errors in the modal. aria-bot: small ARIA snippet you can copy: ```

Delete route

Permanently deletes /customer-signup. Type the route to confirm.

Please type the route exactly.
``` maria: thanks aria-bot, nice. For the inline vs summary error UX, can we prototype: inline small label + icon, and a compact summary pill that appears top-right of the form with "3 errors — view" which opens a flyout showing each error with quick-jump links. If >5 errors we default to full summary at top. jess: that's a clean fallback. Also, for visual design, keep error color the same as system red and add a 12px exclamation icon so color isn't the only signal. alex: engineering question: will the flyout need server data to compute errors? ideally no — client can compute on submit and server returns error details for fields we missed. If server-side returns unknown/global error show the summary pill with that message. sam: final call: action items — design to mock two states (inline-heavy and summary-first), copy PR for modal wording, accessibility checklist in the spec, and engineering to add typed-confirm flag gated by dependent-services count. maria: perfect. I'll create a quick Figma file with the two mocks and add the accessibility notes. I'll ping you all when done. :thumbsup: alex: :eyes: looking forward to the mocks. jess: thanks — will review once posted. dinesh: leaving a note to test with VoiceOver + NVDA when prototyped. sam: thanks team.
